title: Counting slowly to calm down
examples: Does counting to ten help me calm down?
How do I count to calm?
What can I do when I am angry?

explain.say: Here is a calm-down tool you can use anywhere: counting! Look at the board. A number line from zero to ten. Each hop is one number. Let us hop slowly, together.
Count each hop with one slow breath. One, breathe. Two, breathe. Three, breathe. Do not rush. Slow counting tells your body to slow down too. Can you get to ten with me?

Here is a fun one. Count back from ten, like a rocket. Ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two, one, zero. Blast off into calm! Counting back keeps your brain busy, so the big feeling gets smaller. Which do you like best?
See the feelings meter? The needle is at cross. Hot face, fast heart. That is a good time to count. You can count in your head, so nobody knows. When could you use counting?

faq.q: How does counting help me calm down?
faq.a: Counting gives your brain a simple job, and slow counting slows your breathing. That helps the big feeling get smaller.
asks: Tell me about Count to ten

faq.q: When should I count to calm?
faq.a: When you feel cross, worried or wobbly, before the feeling gets too big. You can count in your head anywhere.

faq.q: Can I count higher than ten?
faq.a: Yes. If you still feel cross at ten, keep going to twenty, or count back again.
asks: What if ten is not enough?

faq.q: Can I count in another language?
faq.a: Yes! Counting in another language makes your brain work a little harder, which can help even more. Try uno, dos, tres, or ichi, ni, san.

faq.q: What if counting does not help?
faq.a: Try another tool, like belly breathing or a calm corner. You can say, I need help. A grown-up you trust can help.

facts: Counting from 0 to 10 in hops of one takes ten hops.
Counting in your head is a calming tool you can use without anyone noticing.

quiz.say: You count back from ten. What number comes after seven?
quiz.show: Counting back: what comes after seven?
quiz.why: Counting back goes down by one: seven, then six.

wrong.1: Eight is counting up. Counting back goes down.
wrong.2: Five skips six. Go one at a time.

quiz.say: How fast should you count to calm down?
quiz.why: Slow counting with breaths tells your body to slow down.

wrong.1: Fast counting can keep your body fizzy.
wrong.2: Every number gets a slow breath.
